body: Well, the [CSS definition of "inert"](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui-4/#inert) describes what it means for something to be inert (e.g. act as if pointer-events is none). But perhaps you're talking about the [CSS definition of `interactivity`](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui-4/#propdef-interactivity). CSS does define that, but it leaves the behavior to the host language: "The element’s inertness is determined by the host language. (This will usually mean the element is not inert.)". So the intention of this section was to provide the ways HTML makes things "inert", namely the behavior in CSS's parenthetical, plus the special behavior for modal dialogs.
